categoryName: Confectionery — chocolate, candy, gum, mints, ice cream

skuLines.line: Everyday milk chocolate bars — impulse ₹10/₹20 packs
skuLines.examples: Cadbury Dairy Milk 13.2g/23g, Cadbury 5 Star 19g/35g, Nestlé Munch 10g/18.7g, Cadbury Perk 13g
skuLines.packSizes: 10g–35g single bars; distributor cases of 24/48/60; retail hanger strips
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; dips Jun–Jul (school vacation), spikes on parents' visiting days, exam weeks and festival distribution
skuLines.marginBand: 8–14% retailer gross (branded chocolate is the thinnest margin in the store; the volume driver, not the earner)
skuLines.notes: Highest-rotation line in the whole category — never allow an out-of-stock. Shelf life 6–9 months. Melt/bloom on the Chandigarh–Nahan–Rajgarh leg Apr–Jun is the #1 quality complaint: order in night-dispatch or reefer, cut order size in peak summer, and refuse bloomed stock at the gate rather than shelving it. Hill winter (Nov–Feb) is actually ideal storage.

skuLines.examples: Nestlé KitKat 2-finger 12.8g & 4-finger 27.5g, Cadbury Perk, Nestlé Munch, Amul Dark Passion Wafer 300g
skuLines.packSizes: 12g–35g singles; 4-finger 27.5g; multipacks of 3/5; Amul 300g family wafer
skuLines.notes: Wafer bars survive hill transport better than solid moulded bars (less visible bloom) — a good summer substitute when solid-bar quality is at risk. Shelf life 6–9 months.

skuLines.line: Mid-size milk chocolate bars — the ₹40–₹100 self-treat
skuLines.examples: Cadbury Dairy Milk 50g, Dairy Milk Silk 55–60g, Nestlé Munch Max, Amul Milk Chocolate 40g/75g
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes at month-start (staff salary), Raksha Bandhan, Diwali, Gurpurab, annual-day and birthdays
skuLines.notes: The workhorse for university students and staff. Silk needs the coolest shelf in the store — it is the softest-tempered mass bar and shows heat damage first.

skuLines.line: Large sharing / family chocolate bars & home-pack pouches
skuLines.examples: Dairy Milk Silk 150g, Dairy Milk 165g Home Treats, Amul Milk Chocolate 150g (₹180 MRP), Nestlé Munch/KitKat multipack pouch
skuLines.seasonality: Festivals, birthdays, hostel-room sharing, exam-end celebrations
skuLines.notes: Married-staff families with children are the buyer here, not the hostel child. Amul's own large-format bars are verified at ₹180/150g and carry a better margin than Mondelez/Nestlé equivalents.

skuLines.examples: Cadbury Gems 15.8g/40g, Cadbury Nutties, Cadbury Choco Fills, Nestlé Munch Pop Choc
skuLines.notes: Sugar-shelled — the single most heat-tolerant chocolate format. Make this the summer anchor when bars are at melt risk. Sub-5-year-olds: small buttons are a mild choking item, sell the pouch not the loose piece.

skuLines.examples: Cadbury Bournville 80g, Amul 55% Dark 150g, Amul Tropical Orange 55% Dark, Amul Fruit-n-Nut 55% Dark
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; grows steadily as a health-led purchase
skuLines.notes: Dark chocolate is the fastest-shifting health preference in Indian chocolate (IMARC/EMR both flag it). Longer shelf life (9–12 months) and far better heat tolerance than milk — a low-risk hill SKU. Amul verified ₹360 per 150g×2 pack.

skuLines.line: Premium / craft high-cocoa dark chocolate (70%+, bean-to-bar, no-added-sugar)
skuLines.examples: Amul 90% Bitter 150g, Amul 99% Cacao 125g, Amul India-Origin Dark, The Whole Truth 70–92% bars, Lindt Excellence 70%/85%
skuLines.notes: A small, deliberate shelf (6–10 facings) — carries 2–3× the margin of a mass bar and stops the salary-earning staff wallet leaking on the town trip. Slow-moving: order small, watch expiry, 12-month shelf life helps. Confirm every craft bar is veg (green dot) and dairy-source acceptable.

skuLines.line: Imported / global bars, pralines and countlines
skuLines.examples: Snickers 22g/45g, Mars, Bounty, Toblerone, Ferrero Rocher T4, Hershey's Kisses 33g/100g, Lindt
skuLines.seasonality: Gifting Oct–Dec, Valentine-adjacent Feb (low relevance on a school campus), parents' visiting days
skuLines.notes: HARD SCREEN for this campus: no liqueur/rum-and-raisin/brandy-filled chocolate (alcohol), and check gelatin/beef derivatives on imported novelty lines — several imported gummy-in-chocolate SKUs are non-veg. Ferrero Rocher is heat-fragile: do not stock May–Jun.

skuLines.examples: Cadbury Celebrations (₹100–₹1,200 range), Cadbury Silk Pralines, Ferrero Rocher T16, Amul gift packs
skuLines.seasonality: ~70% of Indian confectionery sales cluster around festivals: Diwali, Raksha Bandhan, Gurpurab, Lohri, annual day, staff farewells, teachers' day
skuLines.marginBand: 10–18% plus manufacturer festive scheme (the scheme, not the base margin, is where the money is)
skuLines.notes: Chocolate boxes have largely replaced mithai as the Indian gift (IMARC). Buy on the festive scheme window and pre-book 6–8 weeks ahead — hill resupply mid-festival is not realistic. Dead stock after the festival is the whole risk: take return/rotation terms in writing.

skuLines.line: Kids novelty chocolate with a toy / surprise
skuLines.examples: Kinder Joy 20g, Cadbury Gems Surprise ball, chocolate-with-toy pouches
skuLines.notes: Kinder Joy is India-veg (milk, no egg) and needs cool storage — it slumps above 25°C. Toy component: keep the under-3 warning visible; married-staff families with toddlers are a real cohort here.

skuLines.line: Mild milk / white chocolate for young children
skuLines.examples: Nestlé Milkybar, Amul Chocominis 250g (₹130), Amul Velvette Milk, Lacto-style milk bars
skuLines.notes: The line parents of 3–7 year-olds actually ask for — no caffeine, no hard pieces, low choking risk. Amul Chocominis 250g at ₹130 verified: the best value-per-gram kids format on the shelf and a strong repack/pick-and-mix source.

skuLines.examples: Cadbury Nutties, Amul Almondo (chocolate-coated almonds), chocolate-coated raisins/cashews, chocolate-coated makhana
skuLines.notes: Reads as 'healthier' to staff and elderly, so it defends price. Panned coating survives hill transport well. Watch rancidity on nut lines — 6-month shelf life, first-in-first-out strictly.

skuLines.examples: Lotte Choco Pie 6pc/12pc, Britannia Chocolush/pie-format, Mondelez Oreo Cakester
skuLines.notes: A hostel-room staple: shelf-stable, shareable, no fridge. Confirm the marshmallow is veg/pectin — gelatin marshmallow is unacceptable on this campus. Shelf life ~6 months, crushes easily: do not bottom-load cartons on the hill route.

skuLines.examples: Nutella 180g/350g, Hershey's Chocolate Syrup, Amul Chocolate Syrup, Sundrop/Veeba choco-hazelnut spread
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; peaks with the ice cream/milkshake season Apr–Sep
skuLines.notes: Sits in the chocolate aisle but behaves like grocery. Also the topping input for a softy/shake counter — buy it once, sell it twice.

skuLines.examples: Amul Sugar Free 55% Dark 150g, Sugarless Bliss, jaggery/date-sweetened craft bars, stevia-sweetened dark
skuLines.notes: India's sugar-free confectionery segment is small but compounding (≈USD 72M in 2024 → ≈USD 120M by 2033, IMARC). For diabetic staff and the elderly, 2–4 facings is enough — this is a 'we have it' line, not a volume line, and its absence is exactly the kind of gap that sends a family shopping in town.

skuLines.line: ₹1 / ₹0.50 hard-boiled fruit candy — the loose jar
skuLines.examples: Parle Mango Bite, Parle Kaccha Mango Bite, Parle Orange Candy, Alpenliebe, Parle Melody
skuLines.packSizes: Jars of 100–300 pieces; ₹1 and ₹5 pillow packs; 1kg pouches
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; the single most stable line in the category
skuLines.marginBand: 18–28% (jars bought on a case scheme reach 30%+)
skuLines.notes: This IS the pocket-money economy of a residential school — the ₹1/₹5 price point is where Perfetti and Parle deliberately keep volume. Shelf life 12–18 months, humidity is the enemy: heavy Sirmaur monsoon makes boiled candy sticky and clumped, so keep jars sealed with silica and never store on a floor slab.

skuLines.examples: Cadbury Choclairs Gold, Chocoliebe Eclairs Plus (Perfetti), Parle 2-in-1 Eclairs, Nestlé Munch éclairs
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; large spike whenever the Academy/Trust distributes at an event
skuLines.notes: The default 'change-counter' and event-distribution candy. Softer centre than boiled candy — keeps better in a cold hill store than in the plains, but do not stack near a heater in winter.

skuLines.examples: Lotte Coffy Bite, Parle Kismi Toffee Bar, Lotte Lacto King, Nestlé Milkybar Choo, Alpenliebe Creamfills
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; milk/lacto formats do better in winter
skuLines.notes: Coffee toffee skews to staff and university; lacto/milk toffee to the youngest children. Both are 12-month shelf life and monsoon-sensitive to stickiness.

skuLines.examples: Chupa Chups ₹10, Alpenliebe Pop, Center Fruit Pop, Chocoliebe Pop
skuLines.notes: Counter-top display jar is the whole merchandising trick — it must sit at child eye-level. CHOKING: keep the under-3 caution in mind for staff families; the stick is the safety feature, do not de-stick for a repack.

skuLines.examples: Alpenliebe Juzt Jelly (25% fruit pulp), Perfetti Marbels, Sunfeast/ITC jelly, Indian pectin gummy bears
skuLines.notes: NON-NEGOTIABLE SCREEN: gummies are the highest-risk category for animal gelatin. Stock pectin/starch/veg-gelling agents only, green dot verified on the label — a beef-gelatin gummy on a Kalgidhar Trust campus is a reputational incident, not a stock error. Rules out most imported gummy brands.

skuLines.examples: DS Group Pulse & Pulse Natkaare, Center Shock (Perfetti), imli/nimbu candy, kachcha aam sour candy
skuLines.notes: Pulse built a ₹100 cr+ brand on exactly this teen/pre-teen cohort — a residential school of 5–18 year-olds is its ideal catchment. Regional desi flavours (imli, kachcha aam, masala) outsell Western sour formats here.

skuLines.examples: Dabur Hajmola (regular/imli/chatpata), anardana goli, amla candy, Nutraj/Patanjali amla candy, ajwain goli
skuLines.packSizes: ₹1/₹5 sachets; bottles of 60/120 tablets; 100g–400g amla candy jars
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes after festival/langar heavy meals
skuLines.notes: In an Indian institutional store this out-turns most chocolate lines and nobody plans for it. Amla candy has a genuine local-sourcing angle (Himachal amla/apricot) at 30–50% margin. Kept as food, not medicine — no drug licence needed for candy-format churan.

skuLines.examples: Vicks cough drops, Halls, Strepsils, Cofsils, Cofitos (Perfetti), Nilgiri/tulsi/mint drops
skuLines.priceBand: ₹1–₹5 per piece; ₹50 per strip; ₹150–₹300 per jar
skuLines.seasonality: HEAVY spike Oct–Mar (cold hill winter) and through the monsoon cough season; near-dead May–Jun
skuLines.notes: For a cold, high-altitude campus of 5,000 people this is arguably the most essential single line in the whole confectionery lane — a residential school in a Himachal winter runs on it. Strepsils/Cofsils sit at the pharmacy/confectionery boundary: plain lozenges are food, medicated antiseptic ones may need a drug-licence check depending on the SKU. Pre-build stock in September; the monsoon-damaged road is not the time to discover you are out.

skuLines.examples: Nestlé Polo, Mentos (Perfetti), Smint, Chlormint, Minto, Happydent mints
skuLines.packSizes: ₹5/₹10 rolls; 20–50g tubes; bottles of 60–100; jars of 100+
skuLines.notes: Breath-freshening demand on a campus with classroom/staff-room contact is constant. 18-month shelf life, indifferent to hill transport — the lowest-risk line in the category. Bottle/tube formats give the staff cohort a ₹100+ basket item.

skuLines.line: Mukhwas & saunf mouth freshener (tobacco-free, no supari/pan masala)
skuLines.examples: Loose saunf-mishri, dhania-dal mukhwas, Chandan/Tulsi mukhwas sachets, mint-coated saunf
skuLines.notes: HARD LINE: tobacco-free and supari-free only. Exclude pan masala outright (Rajnigandha and every pan-masala-branded SKU) — a Sikh institutional campus and a no-tobacco policy make even the adjacency wrong. Plain saunf/mishri/dhania mukhwas is traditional, wholly acceptable, and the best-margin item on this shelf when bought loose and repacked.

skuLines.examples: Center Fresh, Happydent (Perfetti), Chlormint gum, Wrigley's Orbit, Boomer
skuLines.packSizes: ₹1/₹2 singles; ₹5/₹10 packs; bottles of 25–60 pellets; jars of 100+
skuLines.notes: Check the Academy's own rule before ranging deep: many residential schools restrict gum (uniforms, floors, desks). Range it primarily for university students and staff, keep the child-facing facings shallow, and let the warden's policy set the depth rather than guessing.

skuLines.examples: Perfetti Big Babol, Center Fruit, Boomer, Bubbaloo
skuLines.notes: Purely the 5–14 cohort. Same school-policy caveat as gum, more strongly — if the Academy bans it, this line goes to zero regardless of demand, so confirm before committing a case.

skuLines.line: Chikki, gajak, revdi & til-gud (winter jaggery confectionery)
skuLines.examples: Peanut chikki, til chikki, gud-patti, Lohri gajak, revdi, Krishna/Bikano gajak
skuLines.seasonality: STRONGLY seasonal: Nov–Feb, peaking at Lohri and Makar Sankranti; nearly unsellable Apr–Sep
skuLines.notes: In a cold Himachal township this is the winter sweet, and a store that misses it is failing at the one moment it has an unbeatable local edge. Sourceable regionally (Punjab/HP gajak makers) — buy loose, repack, keep the margin. Short shelf life (2–3 months, goes soft in humidity): buy in three waves through the season, not one.

skuLines.line: Fruit leather & local fruit candy (aam papad, imli, apricot, plum)
skuLines.examples: Aam papad slabs/rolls, imli candy, Himachali dried apricot/plum candy, amla-anardana bites
skuLines.seasonality: Apricot/plum after the Jul–Aug HP harvest; aam papad year-round
skuLines.notes: The clearest local-sourcing win in the category — Sirmaur/Shimla belt apricot, plum and amla can be bought within the district instead of trucked from the plains, which cuts freight and raises margin at the same time. No cold chain, 4–6 month shelf life, but humidity-sensitive: sealed packs only in monsoon.

skuLines.examples: Pectin/agar marshmallows, marshmallow twists, packaged candy floss, sugar-toy novelty
skuLines.seasonality: Birthdays, annual day, sports day, fêtes
skuLines.notes: Same gelatin screen as gummies — almost all mainstream marshmallow is gelatin-based, so veg/agar/pectin only. Crushes and cakes in humidity; small orders.

skuLines.line: Bulk festival & event distribution toffee pouches
skuLines.examples: 1kg Alpenliebe/Mango Bite/éclairs pouches, mixed-toffee institutional bags, Celebrations bulk cartons
skuLines.packSizes: 500g / 1kg pouches; cases of 6–12 pouches; 200–500 piece bags
skuLines.cohort: all (institutional buyer: the Academy, the University, the Trust)
skuLines.seasonality: Gurpurab, Diwali, Lohri, annual day, sports day, prize distribution, Children's Day, exam results, farewells
skuLines.marginBand: 12–22% (thin per-unit, but the largest single-bill line in the category)
skuLines.notes: This is the institutional half of the category and it is what makes confectionery matter beyond pocket money: one Academy event moves more candy than a fortnight of the counter. Needs a standing pre-order rhythm with the school office 3–4 weeks before each event, and it should be invoiced institutionally rather than rung through the retail POS.

skuLines.line: Loose pick-and-mix candy counter (own repack, by weight)
skuLines.examples: Mixed toffee/éclairs/boiled candy weighed out; 100g/250g/500g own bags
skuLines.packSizes: Sold by weight, 50g upward; sourced from 1kg–5kg bulk
skuLines.marginBand: 30–45% — the highest-margin construct in the whole category
skuLines.notes: Buy branded candy in 1kg+ bulk, sell by weight from a clean dispenser. Needs a weighing scale, food-grade bags and a legal-metrology-compliant label (net weight, price, date) if pre-packed. Monsoon humidity is the operational risk — small batches, sealed bulk, silica in the dispensers.

skuLines.examples: Sugar-free mints, sugar-free lozenges, stevia/isomalt boiled candy, sugar-free chocolate mints
skuLines.notes: 2–4 facings. A campus with resident elderly and long-serving staff will have diabetics who currently buy nothing from this aisle; the point is coverage, not volume. Slow-moving with 18-month shelf life, so the carrying cost is low.

skuLines.line: Candy-toy combos & birthday return-gift party packs
skuLines.examples: Candy-with-toy pouches, whistle/pop candy, assembled return-gift bags, candle + candy party kits
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round birthdays; peaks at term time, dead in vacation
skuLines.notes: Assembling the bag is the value-add — a hostel child's birthday or a staff family's party currently means a trip to town. Bundle with the ice cream cake pre-order below and it becomes one order instead of a lost sale. Choking-hazard labelling on small toys for under-3 siblings.

skuLines.line: Ice lollies & low-price frozen sticks (₹10 opening price point)
skuLines.examples: Kwality Wall's Trixy, Amul orange bar / Frostik, Cola/Pepsi bar, generic ice lolly
skuLines.notes: The ₹10 frozen entry point is what a school child can actually afford daily — it, not the cone, is the volume driver of the freezer. Water-ice tolerates freezer-temperature wobble far better than dairy ice cream, so it is also the safest SKU when hill power cuts hit. Cheapest cold-chain risk in the category.

skuLines.examples: Amul Chocobar, Kwality Wall's Feast, Vadilal Badabite, Cream Bell chocobar
skuLines.notes: Core impulse. Coating cracks and 'sweats' if the cold chain breaks even once between the depot and Rajgarh — insist on a reefer or an insulated box with dry ice on the hill leg, and reject any consignment arriving soft. Freezer shelf life 6–9 months but refreeze damage is visible and kills repeat purchase.

skuLines.examples: Kwality Wall's Cornetto, Amul Tricone/Chocolate cone, Vadilal Flingo cone
skuLines.notes: The university-student and staff format. Cones are the most fragile frozen SKU on a hill road — the wafer goes soggy the moment the cold chain lapses. Do not over-order relative to freezer capacity; a soggy Cornetto is a lost customer, not a markdown.

skuLines.examples: Amul vanilla/butterscotch/chocolate cup, Vadilal cup, Kwality Wall's cup, Mother Dairy cup
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Sep peak; the format that survives best off-season (dessert-after-dinner use)
skuLines.notes: Spoon-in-lid cups are the most forgiving frozen format for a canteen — stackable, no coating to crack, easy to serve. Keep vanilla and butterscotch permanently; they are half of Indian cup volume.

skuLines.examples: Magnum (almond/classic), Amul Epic/Belgian chocolate bar, Cornetto Selection
skuLines.notes: Premium impulse and artisanal is the fastest-growing slice of a 15% CAGR ice cream market (EMR). Shallow depth (4–8 units), but it captures the salaried wallet that otherwise waits for a town trip. Needs the coldest, most stable part of the freezer.

skuLines.examples: Amul kulfi, matka/malai kulfi, kesar-pista kulfi, Vadilal kulfi, Gourmet gulab jamun/falooda/kesar-rasmalai tubs
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Sep; also holds up at festivals and functions year-round better than Western formats
skuLines.notes: Culturally the strongest frozen line for the staff/family/elderly cohorts — Vadilal's Gourmet Natural range is built on exactly these desi flavours. Denser than ice cream, so it survives a short cold-chain lapse better than a cone.

skuLines.examples: Amul 700ml/1L tub, Vadilal 1L family pack, Kwality Wall's 700ml, Mother Dairy brick
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Sep; plus functions, birthdays and guest visits year-round
skuLines.notes: Take-home dominates Indian ice cream volume (EMR) and married-staff quarters are exactly that buyer. Occupies the most freezer litres per rupee of margin, so cap the range — 4–6 SKUs (vanilla, butterscotch, chocolate, strawberry, kesar-pista, tutti-frutti) covers 80% of demand. 4L catering packs serve the canteens and events.

skuLines.examples: Amul 6-chocobar pack, Kwality Wall's multipack, Vadilal 8-bar family box
skuLines.notes: Better basket value than singles and better freezer economics per rupee than tubs. The natural pack for a staff family with two or three children — it converts a daily ₹20 visit into one ₹200 bill.

skuLines.examples: Amul ice cream cake, Vadilal/Cream Bell ice cream cake, 4L party brick with topping
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round birthdays and farewells; term-time only
skuLines.notes: Runs on pre-order, not stock — 24–48 hours' notice through the hostel warden or the staff-quarters WhatsApp, ordered onto the next inbound cold run. Zero spoilage risk when it is sold before it is bought, and it is the single clearest 'we saved you a trip to town' offer in the category.

skuLines.examples: Cream Bell frozen dessert, Vadilal frozen dessert, regional frozen-dessert tubs
skuLines.notes: Cheaper per litre than dairy ice cream and more tolerant of temperature swings — a rational hedge for a location with power cuts and a long cold-chain leg. Must be labelled 'frozen dessert', not 'ice cream' (FSSAI); it is vegetable fat, so declare it plainly rather than letting a buyer assume dairy. Note the industry is moving the other way — Kwality Wall's has said it will be all-dairy by 2027.

skuLines.line: Soft-serve / softy premix, wafer cones & sundae toppings
skuLines.examples: Softy premix powder (vanilla/chocolate/strawberry), wafer cones in bulk, chocolate/strawberry sauce, sprinkles, crushed nuts
skuLines.packSizes: 1kg premix packs; 100/200-count cone cartons; 1kg sauce jars
skuLines.priceBand: ₹300–₹900 per premix kg; ₹250–₹600 per cone carton
skuLines.marginBand: 45–60% at the counter — by far the best margin in the frozen lane
skuLines.notes: Only worth it if a canteen or the Ary Lite counter runs a softy machine. Premix is shelf-stable, so it dodges the cold-chain problem entirely: the freight risk sits on a powder, not on frozen stock. Needs a machine, daily cleaning discipline and FSSAI-compliant handling; the payoff is the highest gross margin per rupee of anything discussed here.

skuLines.line: Ice candy tubes & frozen jelly pops (₹5–₹10)
skuLines.examples: Ice candy tubes, frozen jelly pops, DIY freeze-at-home ice candy packs
skuLines.notes: The absolute cheapest frozen unit — matters because it is the only frozen item the youngest school children can buy from their own pocket money. Sold unfrozen as a multipack it needs no cold chain at all, which makes it the one frozen-adjacent line that is immune to the hill logistics problem.

trends2026: Cocoa-cost inflation is being managed through price-pack architecture rather than sticker prices: grammage cuts on mass bars and a deliberate push of ₹5 and ₹10 SKUs (Perfetti has said it is balancing its portfolio around exactly those two price points). For a campus store this means the ₹10 shelf keeps working, but the gram-per-rupee quietly falls each year and the ₹20 pack becomes the real value unit.

Health-led premiumisation in chocolate: dark, high-cocoa, no-added-sugar, jaggery/date-sweetened and Indian bean-to-bar. Amul now retails 55%, 90% and 99% cacao bars and a sugar-free 55% dark; India's sugar-free confectionery segment is tracked at roughly USD 72M (2024) rising to USD 120M (2033). Dark also happens to be the most heat- and transport-tolerant chocolate, which suits a hill supply line.

Desi-flavour innovation across both chocolate and sugar candy — cardamom, jaggery, masala chai, mango, tamarind and spice profiles blended into modern formats. Regional/tangy candy (Pulse, kachcha aam, imli) outsells Western sour formats in Indian small-town retail.

Quick commerce has reset expectations of assortment breadth even where it does not deliver: online was already over 10% of HUL's ice cream business by 2023, and convenience stores now hold the largest single share of Indian candy distribution (34.2%). A closed township with no q-commerce coverage is a captive market — but residents benchmark the shelf against what their phone shows them.

Ice cream is premiumising fast on a ~15% CAGR (USD 3.98bn in 2025 → USD 16.1bn by 2035): artisanal and gelato-style, Western flavours (matcha, tiramisu, salted caramel) alongside desi tubs (gulab jamun, falooda, kesar-rasmalai), and low-sugar/dairy-free variants. Simultaneously the dairy-versus-frozen-dessert line is hardening — Kwality Wall's has committed to all-dairy ice cream by 2027, which will pull the cheap vegetable-fat tier out of the market.

Functional gummies (vitamin C, multivitamin, melatonin, immunity) are moving candy into the wellness aisle — and are driving explicit 'veg/pectin, no gelatin' labelling, which is exactly the claim this campus needs anyway.

Chocolate has largely displaced mithai as the default Indian gift; roughly 70% of Indian confectionery sales cluster around festivals, and boxed formats hold about half the chocolate market. Gifting is a pre-booked, scheme-driven, calendar-locked business, not a shelf business.

Clean-label and protein crossover: chocolate-coated protein bars, 'no palm oil / no maida / no refined sugar' claims and craft brands (The Whole Truth) that price a bar at ₹150–₹350 and get it. This is where the premium end of the shelf is being redefined, well above the traditional ₹100 ceiling.
adjacentServices: Brand-placed deep freezer / visi-cooler on an exclusivity or placement contract (Amul, Kwality Wall's, Vadilal) — frozen range with near-zero capex, and the brand's own service engineer becomes responsible for the asset in a location where a technician is 40 km away.
Soft-serve / softy and milkshake counter at a canteen or the Ary Lite point — 45–60% gross margin, and the premix is shelf-stable so the freight risk sits on a powder rather than on frozen stock.

Birthday, farewell and function desk: pre-ordered ice cream cake plus candles, party candy and an assembled return-gift bag, taken 24–48 hours ahead through hostel wardens and the staff-quarters group, and ridden in on the next scheduled cold run. Sold before it is bought, so zero spoilage.

Institutional festival and event supply to the Academy, the University and the Trust — bulk distribution toffee and gift boxes for Gurpurab, Diwali, Lohri, annual day, sports day, prize distribution and results, pre-booked 3–4 weeks out and invoiced institutionally rather than rung through the retail till.

Pick-and-mix weigh counter — branded candy bought in 1kg+ bulk and sold loose at 30–45% margin, plus loose mukhwas and locally-sourced chikki/apricot candy. Needs a scale and legal-metrology-compliant labels on anything pre-packed.
In-store chocolate gift hamper assembly for parents' visiting days and staff Diwali gifting — converts thin-margin bought-in boxes into a made-up basket the buyer cannot get in town.

Consolidated cold-chain milk run: put ice cream on the existing dairy/curd inbound reefer instead of buying a separate frozen leg — the single highest-leverage fix for the Rajgarh hill route, especially Apr–Jun and through monsoon road closures.

Unattended candy tray / honesty box or a small vending point in hostel common rooms and staff blocks, replenished from the main store — extends the ₹1–₹20 pocket-money shelf to where the children actually are, after store hours.

Student card / hostel ledger tie-in so children buy against a parent-funded balance rather than cash — the mechanism that lets a residential school of 5–18 year-olds spend at all, and it produces per-child spend data the Academy will want.
